# Attempt 2: what the triage's 0.52 actually was

The review triage returned the ticket for two criteria. Criterion 1 was a real absence and is amended
at record 22. Criterion 3, answered no at 0.52 against 0.48, was not a legibility problem: the
implementer read `harness/loop.py` against the criterion's five named conditions and found the
evidence genuinely partial. `StopTest` covered all six reason strings in `[run] stops`, which is why
nothing in attempt 1 refused, and the criterion names five conditions rather than six strings.

What was true before attempt 2, with the reason per condition rather than a verdict:

| Condition | Reason | Before |
|---|---|---|
| a gate that refuses | `gate_refused` | declaration only: `advance` raises and appends nothing, so there is no record to find |
| a Jev question that does not clear | `question_open` | detecting the wrong thing: the `open_questions` list in the clarify draft file. A `decision` record below its threshold was invisible and the loop kept offering the same `advance` |
| a failed check | `check_failed` | detected from the journal |
| red CI | `ci_red` | declaration only: nothing read CI before `verify-delivery` refused |
| a second return on the same slice | `second_return` | detected from the journal |

Two of five detected, one detecting something else, two declarations. So the triage was right and the
0.52 was the closest thing to a correct probability in this journal: the criterion asks for five
conditions each reporting the stage, the record and one resume command, and two of them could not be
reported at all unless a session remembered to declare them.

Closed in attempt 2, RED at record 23 and GREEN at record 24, both declaring `--model opus --agent
seen-implementer`: `unclear_decision()` finds a blocking question answered on record and below its bar
for the stage and attempt in hand and stops at `question_open`, pointing at the decision record and
naming the question to answer again, with `harness decide` as the resume rather than a note, because a
note leaves the same answer on record and the advance refuses identically; `ci_red()` reads the
completed check runs GitHub already reports and stops at `deliver` before offering the draft, while
pending, no runs and an unavailable `gh` are deliberately not this stop; and `DETECTED` and `DECLARED`
name the classification in the module rather than only in the test, so the two that can only be
declared are declared honestly and are still held to the vocabulary.

The RED's own words, on the two that mattered: "A Jev question that does not clear is one of the five
conditions the criterion names, and the answer on record cannot pass the gate it blocks, so offering
advance again is retrying a decision", and "Red CI is one of the five conditions the criterion names,
and it is readable from what verify-delivery already reads, so the run must not offer draft and wait
for a session to declare the stop".

One definition was extracted rather than duplicated: `cli.decision_refuses(stage, answer)` now says
which way a blocking question reads, and the gate and the loop both read it.

Three things named and left, beside the three already on record at 12 and 16. The gate's own refusal
message still says to record a note and advance again, which is right for an answer Jev gave inside
the advance and wrong for one already in the journal, where `recorded_decisions` reuses it and the
advance refuses identically: the loop's resume says `decide` and the gate's message does not, so the
same honesty has two wordings. `_second_return` counts returns from the accepted plan rather than per
slice, so two returns on one slice with a replan between them would reset the count. And `harness run`
at the deliver stage now makes one `gh api` read per invocation, recorded nowhere and with every error
swallowed; the tests never reach the network because the delivery walk already stubs the check runs.
